mcqs.question: What is a recessive trait in genetics?

options.A: A trait that is expressed only when an individual has two identical alleles for that trait.
options.B: A trait that is expressed only when an individual has one dominant and one recessive allele.
options.C: A trait that is always expressed regardless of allele combination.
options.D: A trait that determines the sex of an organism.

mcqs.answer: A trait that is expressed only when an individual has two identical alleles for that trait.
mcqs.explanation: A recessive trait is expressed only when both alleles at a locus are recessive (homozygous recessive). In the presence of a dominant allele, the recessive trait is masked. Option A correctly captures this definition, whereas the other options describe dominant traits, unrelated concepts, or are inaccurate.

mcqs.question: In a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous pea plants (Rr × Rr) for a single trait, what phenotypic ratio is expected in the F2 generation?
mcqs.explanation: A monohybrid cross of two heterozygotes (Rr × Rr) yields genotypes RR, Rr, rR, and rr in a 1:2:1 ratio. The dominant phenotype (RR, Rr) appears in three of the four possibilities, giving a phenotypic ratio of 3 dominant : 1 recessive. The other ratios correspond to dihybrid or other crosses.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes genotype from phenotype in a pea plant cross?

options.A: Genotype is the observable trait; phenotype is the genetic makeup.
options.B: Genotype is the genetic makeup (e.g., RR, Rr, rr); phenotype is the observable characteristic (e.g., tall or dwarf).
options.C: Genotype and phenotype are interchangeable terms.
options.D: Genotype refers only to dominant traits.

mcqs.answer: Genotype is the genetic makeup (e.g., RR, Rr, rr); phenotype is the observable characteristic (e.g., tall or dwarf).
mcqs.explanation: Genotype denotes the allele combination an organism carries, while phenotype is the physical expression of those alleles. Option B states this distinction accurately. Options A, C, and D confuse or oversimplify the terms.

mcqs.question: If a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous plants (Rr × Rr) yields 75 tall and 25 dwarf plants, what are the corresponding genotypic ratios?
mcqs.explanation: The cross Rr × Rr gives genotypes in a 1:2:1 ratio: one homozygous dominant (RR), two heterozygous (Rr), and one homozygous recessive (rr). The phenotypic 3:1 ratio (tall : dwarf) reflects that RR and Rr both produce the tall phenotype. Option A correctly states the genotypic ratio.

mcqs.question: Mendel chose pea plants for his experiments because:

options.A: They have a short generation time and produce many offspring with distinct, easily observable traits.
options.B: Each plant possesses only a single trait.
options.C: All pea plants are genetically identical.
options.D: Pea plants do not follow Mendelian inheritance.

mcqs.answer: They have a short generation time and produce many offspring with distinct, easily observable traits.
mcqs.explanation: Pea plants were ideal for Mendel: they grow quickly, yield many seeds, and exhibit clear, contrasting traits (e.g., flower colour, seed shape). This allowed Mendel to track inheritance across generations. Options B, C, and D are factually incorrect.

mcqs.question: In a cross, all offspring show purple flowers while some parents had white flowers. Which statement best defines the dominant trait observed?

options.A: The trait that appears in the phenotype when at least one dominant allele is present.
options.B: The trait that appears only when two recessive alleles are present.
options.C: The trait that never appears in any generation.
options.D: The trait that determines plant height.

mcqs.answer: The trait that appears in the phenotype when at least one dominant allele is present.
mcqs.explanation: A dominant trait is expressed if an individual carries at least one dominant allele (heterozygous or homozygous). In the scenario, purple flower colour is dominant over white. Options B, C, and D misrepresent dominance.

mcqs.question: A student claims that a recessive trait can be seen in the first generation if one parent carries it. Which statement corrects this misconception?

options.A: Recessive traits are expressed only when both alleles are recessive.
options.B: Recessive traits are always expressed regardless of allele combination.
options.C: Recessive traits are dominant over dominant traits.

mcqs.answer: Recessive traits are expressed only when both alleles are recessive.
mcqs.explanation: A recessive phenotype appears only in individuals homozygous for the recessive allele (rr). If a parent carries a recessive allele but the other parent contributes a dominant allele, the offspring will be heterozygous and display the dominant phenotype. Options B, C, and D are incorrect statements about inheritance.

mcqs.question: Why does a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous plants (Rr × Rr) result in a 3:1 phenotypic ratio?

options.A: Because three of the four possible allele combinations produce the dominant phenotype.
options.B: Because recessive alleles are more frequent than dominant alleles.
options.C: Because each parent contributes only dominant alleles.
options.D: Because the genes involved are linked.

mcqs.answer: Because three of the four possible allele combinations produce the dominant phenotype.
mcqs.explanation: The Punnett square for Rr × Rr gives genotypes RR, Rr, rR, and rr. The first three genotypes (RR, Rr, rR) all express the dominant phenotype, giving a 3 (dominant) : 1 (recessive) phenotypic ratio. Options B, C, and D do not explain the observed ratio correctly.
